LayerFS

Ephemeral Workspaces. Durable Shared History.

LayerFS is the substrate under your agents. Each one mounts a complete, writable Workspace over shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed, and goes away.

Get started · Website · Docs · Benchmarks · Video · LayerFS × DSH · Community

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70c25887-86a1-4d81-bd78-571cf1c09a18 > **Status:** [LayerFS 1.1.0](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/releases/tag/v1.1.0), > released as source: the JavaScript API split into `@layerfs/agent`, `@layerfs/backend` > and `@layerfs/runtime` under [`api/`](api/README.md), plus the `layerfs` command. It breaks > code written for 1.0.0; see the [release record](docs/release-notes/1.1.0/README.md). > The results below are 1.0.0's, measured on `main` at `e5c7aaae05`. The Store runs in its Disposable profile only, with no > crash or power-loss durability: use LayerFS for agent work and its history, not > as the only copy of data you cannot rebuild. Since 1.1.0, LayerFS also supports native Windows dsh Live through WSL2 and its own Linux Docker Engine; see the [Windows setup](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/dsh-layerfs#windows-live). ## Try it with LayerFS × DSH

LayerFS runs today through **LayerFS × DSH**, the `dsh-layerfs` plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Agents in a dsh session fork Branches, test them in Sandboxes, merge and publish, and the **Work** and **History** tabs show every agent's Branch, live.

## Core ideas

01 · Ephemeral Computing
Compute exists only while a command runs.
02 · Decentralized Agents
Agents on different computers share one serverless Store.
03 · Multiagent Coordination
One project, many Branches. One Branch, many agents.

04 · Recursive Filesystem
Fork recursively any Commit, at any depth.
05 · Ultra Storage Optimization
157 snapshots of a real project in 100 MB, 19.9× smaller than Btrfs + zstd.
06 · Instant Bootstrap
Dependencies come with every mount. No time lost reinstalling.
**And underneath them** | | Supporting idea | In one line | | --- | --- | --- | | | **[07 · Auto Checkpoints](https://layerfs.ai/docs/core-ideas/#idea-checkpoints)** | Every step an agent takes is a checkpoint to return to. | | | **[08 · Append-only Objects](https://layerfs.ai/docs/core-ideas/#idea-immutable)** | Saved objects are never rewritten. The Store only grows. | | | **[09 · Conflict Rules (`.lww`)](https://layerfs.ai/docs/core-ideas/#idea-lww)** | Name the files that should never conflict. The newest edit wins. | | | **[10 · Big File, Small Edit](https://layerfs.ai/docs/core-ideas/#idea-bigfile)** | An edit costs the size of the edit, not the size of the file. | ## See it run

Agents fork Branches, work in Workspaces inside Sandboxes, commit, merge and publish to main. The history grows as they go.

## Results Every suite ran once on `main` at `e5c7aaae05` through the JavaScript SDK. Each row links to its method, environment and receipts. | Suite | What it measures | LayerFS 1.0.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | [fs-bench](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fs-bench/) | Cloudflare Computer's own twelve-scenario filesystem benchmark, unchanged, same image | **5.20 s vs 8.88 s, 1.71× faster**; faster in 10 of 12 scenarios | | [dsh-dedup](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/dsh-dedup/) | A real project's history, 157 snapshots (4.94 GB of trees), kept as mountable Commits | **100.1 MB vs 1,994.6 MB, 19.9× smaller** than Btrfs + zstd; 156/156 read back | | [pjdfstest](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/pjdfstest/) | POSIX conformance, 8,798 assertions, against kernel overlayfs | **0 unexpected failures**; keeps 76% of overlayfs's passes, every other failure a deliberate format limit | | [fsx](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fsx/) | Random reads, writes, mapped I/O and truncates, every byte checked | **14/14 pass**, 3.06 M ops, 0 miscompares | | [fsstress](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fsstress/) | Four concurrent processes, then Commit, remount and compare | **3,755/3,755 entries identical**; 5.21 GB captured by one Commit in 4.9 s | | [smallfile](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/smallfile/) | 100,000 files of 4 KiB, four threads, against libfuse passthrough | **Faster in 9 of 9 operations**, 1.27×–10.71× | | [mdtest](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/mdtest/) | Metadata create, rename and remove, against libfuse passthrough | 0.86–1.28× with 1 process, 1.21–4.22× with 4 | | [fio](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fio/) | Data I/O bandwidth, against libfuse passthrough | Random read/write mixes 1.49–2.23×; **slower** on sequential write (0.31×), sequential read (0.81×) and random write (0.40×) | One sample per case, seed 1, no best-of. Host: arm64 Mac, Docker Desktop linux/arm64, 8 CPUs, 8.3 GB; host load is recorded per suite. These are release measurements, not a guarantee for your workload. Earlier fs-bench-pro results: [v0.1.4](docs/release-notes/0.1.4/benchmark-closeout.md) · [v0.1.5](docs/release-notes/0.1.5/benchmark-closeout.md) · [v0.1.6](docs/release-notes/0.1.6/benchmark-closeout.md). ## How it works ```text agent tool call ├─ file tool (read, write, edit, grep …) ── SDK, in process ──────► Store └─ Bash ── mount ─► exec ─► commit ─► unmount ▲ └─ Workspace: FUSE view in a Sandbox's daemon ───────────┘ (committed root + its own overlay) ``` - **Store.** One SQLite file holds every Branch, Commit and content object. Each daemon and SDK process opens it directly; there is no database server. - **Branch, Commit, Layer.** A Branch is a writable line of Commits. Publishing a Branch to `main` adds a Layer. Content is chunked and stored once. - **Workspace.** A mount binds the whole committed tree without copying it. Writes go to the Workspace's own overlay until a Commit saves them. Unmount deletes the overlay, never history. - **Conflict.** Two Commits that change the same file are refused with `Conflict`, unless a `.lww` rule says the newest edit wins. ## Prior art LayerFS builds on well-known ideas: layered and union filesystems, copy-on-write snapshots, content-addressed storage and throwaway execution environments. What it adds is putting them together for agents: every tool call gets a full writable tree, and every result becomes a Commit on a Branch in one shared Store. | Prior work | What it shares with LayerFS | Where LayerFS differs | | --- | --- | --- | | **overlayfs, UnionFS, container image layers** | A read-only lower tree with a writable upper layer, which is also where the "layer" name comes from | The upper layer is not just thrown away or kept as a directory: Commit turns it into an immutable snapshot on a Branch, with history, merge and `Conflict`. overlayfs is in the kernel and more complete; LayerFS's FUSE view deliberately omits FIFOs, sockets, device nodes, set-id bits and separate atime/ctime ([pjdfstest](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs-benchmark/blob/main/data/pjdfstest/README.md)) | | **Btrfs and ZFS snapshots, reflinks** | Cheap copy-on-write snapshots that share unchanged data | Sharing is by content, not by extent, so a file that is rewritten in full still stores only its new chunks. On a small-file history of 157 snapshots that gives [19.9× less space than Btrfs + zstd](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs-benchmark/blob/main/data/dsh-dedup/README.md). Btrfs and ZFS also stay cheap for in-place edits of large files, and they are durable, mature kernel filesystems; LayerFS is not ([why Btrfs used more space here](docs/research/layerfs-vs-btrfs-157/REPORT.md#3-why-btrfs-used-more-storage-in-this-workload)) | | **Git worktrees** | One repository, many working copies and branches | A Workspace holds the whole tree, including `.git`, ignored files, dependencies and build output, so a new mount needs no reinstall. Commits happen per tool call, not when someone runs `git commit` | | **[try](https://github.com/binpash/try)** | Run a command against an overlay of your system, then inspect, apply or discard what it changed | `try` works on one machine with one overlay at a time. LayerFS keeps every result as a Commit, and lets many agents branch from any of them and share one Store | | **Apiary and virtual layered file systems** (Potter and Nieh, [USENIX ATC 2010](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenix-atc-10/apiary-easy-use-desktop-application-fault-containment-commodity-operating), [LISA 2011](https://www.usenix.org/legacy/event/lisa11/tech/full_papers/Potter.pdf)) | Ephemeral containers that start instantly over shared layered filesystems | Apiary isolates desktop applications. LayerFS's target is agent tool calls whose results are kept, branched and merged as history | **Use something else** if you need crash or power-loss durability (the Store runs in its Disposable profile only), full POSIX node types, or top sequential I/O bandwidth ([fio](https://layerfs.ai/benchmarks/fio/)). Install step by step: six steps, without an agent These steps take a fresh clone of this repository to LayerFS × DSH in dsh web: first LayerFS itself, then the dsh bundle. Only dsh web is supported. dsh desktop serves the same web client but was not tested. The headless profile composes no preset registry, so it offers no preset; the Host and the bash environment still load there. ### You need | What | For | Notes | |---|---|---| | Node 22.19 or newer, and pnpm | everything | | | A LayerFS checkout at the pinned commit | the SDK, the agent skill, the Linux build | `../layerfs` beside this repository, or `LAYERFS_SOURCE=`; the commit is in [`layerfs.json`](layerfs.json) | | A built deepseek-harness checkout | the client build and dsh itself | `../deepseek-harness` beside this repository, or `DSH_SOURCE=` for the build. In it, `pnpm install && pnpm run build` (its README) | | Docker | Live | Docker Desktop on macOS. It builds LayerFS and runs its Sandboxes | | Network access | step 1 | crates and the base images | Below, `$DSH_LAYERFS` is this repository's absolute path, `$LAYERFS_SOURCE` the LayerFS checkout's and `$DSH` the deepseek-harness checkout's. ### 1. Install LayerFS Live needs three things from the LayerFS checkout: the JavaScript SDK, a Linux build of the daemon and the SDK's native addon, and a runtime image. Nothing is published, so you build them there. **The SDK** is LayerFS #428's three packages in its `api/` folder (`api/agent/sdk`, `api/backend`, `api/runtime`): `@layerfs/agent` (what agents' scripts call), `@layerfs/backend` (background processes, a Workspace's status, storage) and `@layerfs/runtime` (what the Host runs on a LayerFS home: the worker, Init, removal, status). They are plain JavaScript with no dependencies. Run `npm install` once in `$LAYERFS_SOURCE/api` (it only links the three to each other); the Host links them as `link:../../.layerfs/api/agent/sdk`, `…/api/backend` and `…/api/runtime`, and step 2's `pnpm install` first points `.layerfs` at `$LAYERFS_SOURCE`, then makes those links. Only the native addon is built, and a fresh clone has none (`api/binding/layerfs.node`). On macOS and Windows the Host never loads an addon itself: the home's worker runs the Linux build below. On Linux, see step 4. **The `layerfs` command** agents run (`DSH_LAYERFS_CLI`, the Host's wrapper `packages/host/src/agent/cli.js`) runs the checkout's `api/agent/cli/` folder: one `@layerfs/agent` call per command, JSON on stdout ([api/agent/cli/sdk-to-cli.md](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/api/agent/cli/sdk-to-cli.md) on the #428 branch). Run `npm --prefix "$LAYERFS_SOURCE/api/agent/cli" install` once: it only links `api/agent/cli/node_modules/@layerfs/agent` to `api/agent/sdk` and downloads nothing. `pnpm install` and `pnpm test` stop with that command when it is missing. **The Linux build.** Build `layerfs-daemon` and the addon in the Rust 1.85.1 image, from the LayerFS checkout's root so Cargo picks up its [`.cargo/config.toml`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/.cargo/config.toml) (the ARM64 profile). This is the recipe of LayerFS's [benchmark/AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/benchmark/AGENTS.md#environment), with the crates fetched into a Docker volume instead of the host's `~/.cargo/registry`: ```sh cd "$LAYERFS_SOURCE" docker pull rust:1.85.1-bookworm docker volume create layerfs-cargo && docker volume create layerfs-target mkdir -p core/target/cluster2-linux docker run --rm -v "$LAYERFS_SOURCE":/work:ro -v layerfs-cargo:/usr/local/cargo/registry -w /work \ rust:1.85.1-bookworm cargo fetch --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml --locked docker run --rm -v "$LAYERFS_SOURCE":/work:ro -v layerfs-target:/work/core/target/cluster2-linux \ -v layerfs-cargo:/usr/local/cargo/registry:ro -e CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/work/core/target/cluster2-linux -w /work \ rust:1.85.1-bookworm cargo build --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml --offline --locked --release -j 6 \ -p layerfs-node --lib -p layerfs-daemon --bins ``` The fetch takes about 30 seconds; on an arm64 Mac with Docker limited to 8 CPUs a cold release build took about 2.5 minutes at `-j 2` and 65 seconds at `-j 6`. Agents keep every command under 2 minutes: put `timeout 110` before `cargo` inside the container (`… rust:1.85.1-bookworm timeout 110 cargo build …`; macOS has no `timeout` command) and run the same command again until it prints `Finished`, since Cargo keeps what it compiled. Then, still in `$LAYERFS_SOURCE`, gather the build into one folder, the `bundle` (any folder Docker Desktop shares, such as one under your home): ```sh BUNDLE=$HOME/layerfs-linux-build mkdir -p "$BUNDLE/api/agent" docker run --rm -v layerfs-target:/t:ro -v "$BUNDLE":/out rust:1.85.1-bookworm sh -c \ "cp /t/release/layerfs-daemon /out/ && cp /t/release/liblayerfs_node.so /out/layerfs.node && chown $(id -u):$(id -g) /out/layerfs-daemon /out/layerfs.node" cp -R api/package.json api/backend api/runtime "$BUNDLE/api/" cp -R api/agent/sdk "$BUNDLE/api/agent/" ``` That folder serves Linux (`daemon` and `LAYERFS_NATIVE`). **macOS and Windows need a sealed bundle**: the home's worker runs the bundle's `api/runtime/src/worker/server.js` and checks every file against its `manifest.json` before it listens, which only the tool below writes. Instead, LayerFS's [`tools/worktree.py`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/tools/worktree.py) ([parallel worktrees](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/general/parallel-worktrees.md)), run in `$LAYERFS_SOURCE`, does the same with per-checkout caches, and seals the folder with a `manifest.json`. It needs the runtime image below to exist first, and was not tried for this guide: ```sh python3 tools/worktree.py register --worktree "$LAYERFS_SOURCE" --owner dsh \ --build-image rust:1.85.1-bookworm --runtime-image layerfs-352-runtime:node24 --sandbox-image layerfs-352-runtime:node24 python3 tools/worktree.py prepare --resources --platform linux python3 tools/worktree.py build --resources --platform linux --profile release --jobs 6 ``` `build` prints the sealed folder, `~/.cache/layerfs-worktrees//artifacts/build-linux-`, which serves as `bundle`. **The runtime image** is the Linux image Sandboxes and the macOS worker run. The worker runs `node` from it, so it must carry Node, plus whatever your agents' commands run in Workspaces. The one in use is built from [`tools/runtime/Dockerfile`](tools/runtime/Dockerfile): Node 24.21 on Debian bookworm (the daemon's own base), with corepack's pnpm and yarn prepared offline, and the base's git, python3, gcc and make. ```sh docker build -t layerfs-352-runtime:node24 "$DSH_LAYERFS/tools/runtime" docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' layerfs-352-runtime:node24 # the image setting ``` Use the ID your machine prints: the same build can get a different ID in another image store. Images are never pulled for LayerFS (the worker starts with `--pull never`). ### 2. Build the dsh bundle ```sh cd "$DSH_LAYERFS" LAYERFS_SOURCE="$LAYERFS_SOURCE" pnpm install pnpm run build ``` `pnpm install` first runs [`tools/layerfs-source.mjs`](tools/layerfs-source.mjs), which points the `.layerfs` link at `LAYERFS_SOURCE` (default `../layerfs`) and prints whether that checkout is at the pinned commit; see [Where LayerFS comes from](#where-layerfs-comes-from). `pnpm run build` bundles the client into `packages/client/lib/` with the checkout's `tsdown`: `$DSH_SOURCE/node_modules/.bin/tsdown`, else `../deepseek-harness` beside the repository. Prefer an absolute `DSH_SOURCE` path (`DSH_SOURCE="$DSH" pnpm run build`). Relative paths resolve from `packages/client/`, matching the original build command; an empty value uses the default checkout. The launcher passes the resolved absolute path to the client config. If the checkout or its tsdown CLI is missing, the build stops with `tsdown: No such file or directory`. Run it again after changing the client. ### 3. Make a profile Choose a `DSH_HOME` of your own, so your usual `~/.dsh` is not touched, and use its `web` profile. dsh's `plugin` command makes the profile from the shipped `web` template on first use, installs the packages there with pnpm, and adds each one that is a bundle to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`: ```sh export DSH_HOME=$HOME/dsh-layerfs # any empty folder pnpm --dir "$DSH" dsh plugin --profile web add "link:$DSH_LAYERFS/packages/dsh-layerfs" ``` Install `dsh-layerfs` only. The demo bundle `dsh-layerfs-demo` is disabled permanently and is not in this repository. The bundle includes the LayerFS scripted model, switched off; see [Scripted runs](#scripted-runs). The profile is `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/`. Its `package.json` should now read: ```json "dependencies": { "dsh-layerfs": "link:…/dsh-layerfs/packages/dsh-layerfs" }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-layerfs"] } } ``` [Showing lines 1-300 of 738. # LayerFS 研究报告 ## 1. LayerFS 是什么 [Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs)：Rust 写的**面向 AI agent 的分层文件系统 + 版本历史存储**，口号 "Ephemeral Workspaces, Durable Shared History"。v1.1.0，MIT，2k stars。 核心模型(所有概念都是一等公民)： | 概念 | 含义 | |---|---| | **Store** | 单个 SQLite 文件，存所有 Branch/Commit/内容对象，无数据库服务器；内容分块、按内容寻址、全局去重(append-only,永不重写) | | **Branch / Commit / Layer** | Branch 是可写的 Commit 序列；merge 后 publish 到 `main` 会加一个 Layer | | **Workspace** | 一次挂载 = 不复制地绑定整棵已提交树(含 `.git`、`node_modules`、构建产物)，写进自己的 overlay,Commit 时才固化；unmount 即丢弃 overlay、历史不动 | | **Sandbox** | Docker 容器，daemon 在里面以 FUSE 呈现 Workspace,最多 16 个 Workspace | | **Conflict / `.lww`** | 两个 Commit 改同一文件即拒绝，除非 `.lww` 规则声明“最新者胜” | 设计哲学：**每个 tool call 都是一个完整可写文件系统，每次结果都是一个 Commit**。agent 的文件工具(read/write/edit/grep)直接走进程内 SDK 进 Store;Bash 调用走 `mount → exec → commit → unmount` 一次性生命周期。多台机器上的 agent 可共享同一个 serverless Store(直接开同一个 SQLite)。 卖点数据(官方 benchmark,单次采样)：157 个快照 4.94 GB 树只占 100 MB(比 Btrfs+zstd 小 19.9×);fs-bench 比 Cloudflare Computer 基准快 1.71×;fsx/fsstress/pjdfstest 全过。**明确限制**：Disposable profile、无崩溃/断电持久性，顺序写带宽只有 passthrough 的 0.31×——作者自己说“不能重建的数据别只存这里”。 ## 2. DSH 是什么 [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)(`dsh`):DeepSeek 开源的 agent harness,“Everything is a Plugin” 微内核架构，基于 Cordis。提供 web UI(会话、preset、subagent、bash 沙箱、插件系统 `dsh plugin add`)。 ## 3. 怎么结合的:`dsh-layerfs` 插件包 [dsh-layerfs](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/dsh-layerfs) 是一个 **plugin bundle,不改 dsh 任何代码**。设计 issue [#346](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/346),UI 代码从 layerfs 仓库 `dsh/` 目录迁出([#428](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/428)),通过 `layerfs.json` pin 死 LayerFS commit(v1.1.0 `9f97a7ec95`),靠 `.layerfs` 软链接读 LayerFS 源码——因为 LayerFS 什么都不发布到 npm,SDK/daemon/addon 全要本地从源码构建。 ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph dsh["dsh session (web)"] A[agent / subagent
bash 调用] W[Work / History tabs
project chip / LayerFS 页] end subgraph plugin["dsh-layerfs bundle"] H["layerfs-host
注入 DSH_LAYERFS_* 环境变量
/layerfs 路由 + 记录"] C[layerfs-client
读记录画图] P["preset: LayerFS × DSH minimalist
纯 bash + subagent,无 read/write 工具"] end subgraph layerfs["LayerFS"] CLI["layerfs 命令 / JS SDK
每条 bash = 1 次 SDK 调用"] S[(Store · SQLite)] SB[Sandbox · FUSE Workspace] end A -->|DSH_LAYERFS_PROJECT/SDK/CLI/TRACE| H --> CLI CLI --> S CLI --> SB CLI -->|每次调用 = plugin:layerfs/call 记录| H C -->|读回记录,随运行实时播放| W ``` 关键机制： - ** preset 极简主义**：会话只有 bash(+后台任务、subagent、compaction),**没有 read/write/edit 工具**——所有文件操作都逼 agent 走 `layerfs` CLI 或内联 Node 脚本调 JS SDK。persona 里带 SDK cheat-sheet 和工作规则(一人一 Workspace、只有主 agent 能 publish、Conflict 归 merge 者、unmount 所有 Workspace)。 - **环境变量桥接**：dsh 只允许插件设 `DSH_*` 变量，LayerFS 只认 `LAYERFS_*`。Host 给每个 bash 调用注入 `DSH_LAYERFS_PROJECT/SDK/CLI/TRACE` 等，wrapper(`env.js`)把它们映射成 `LAYERFS_*` 再加载真正的 SDK。 - **可观测性闭环**：每次 SDK 调用落一条 `plugin:layerfs/call` 记录进该 agent 自己的 session + journal;client 插件读回这些记录，**Work/History 标签页按真实时间步进播放**每个 agent 的 fork/commit/merge/publish,含 subagent。 - **平台适配全靠 worker**:Linux 原生加载 addon;macOS 跑一个长驻 Linux 容器 `layerfs-worker`,所有 Store 调用都转发进去(含 manifest 校验的 sealed bundle);Windows 用 WSL2 里的 Node worker + WSL 自己的 Docker Engine(拒绝 `/mnt/c`),还提供 `layerfs.cmd` 让 PowerShell 用同样的 CLI。 实测(2026-10-20,1 主 + 7 子 agent,`deepseek-flash`): | | Wayfare(Node 应用) | Quarry(Rust SQL 数据库) | |---|---|---| | 用时 | 56 min | 4 h 16 min | | 历史 | 147 Commits / 31 Branches / 13 Layers | 913 Commits / 56 Branches / 9 Layers | | 存储 | 1.21 MB 存 91.5 MB 快照，27× 去重 | 8.90 GB 存 4.93 TB 快照，**166× 去重** | ## 4. 评价 本质上是**把“多 agent 并发改代码”从共享工作目录的混沌，换成 git 式分支 + 内容寻址快照 + 即时挂载**：agent 之间靠 Branch 隔离、靠 Conflict 显式碰撞、靠 publish 收敛，且依赖和构建产物随挂载而来(不用重装 `node_modules`)。代价是：未发布需全源码构建、只支持 dsh web、Store 无持久性保证、顺序 I/O 慢。它对 dsh 的集成方式(纯 bundle:host 插件 + client 插件 + preset + mock 模型，零 dsh 代码改动)本身也是 dsh “一切皆插件”架构的一个示范案例。

LayerFS 是什么 [Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs)：Rust 写的**面向 AI agent 的分层文件系统 + 版本历史存储**，口号 "Ephemeral Workspaces, Durable Shared History"。v1.1.0，MIT，2k stars。 核心模型(所有概念都是一等公民)： | 概念 | 含义 | |---|---| | **Store** | 单个 SQLite 文件，存所有 Branch/Commit/内容对象，无数据库服务器；内容分块、按内容寻址、全局去重(append-only,永不重写) | | **Branch / Commit / Layer** | Branch 是可写的 Commit 序列；merge 后 publish 到 `main` 会加一个 Layer | | **Workspace** | 一次挂载 = 不复制地绑定整棵已提交树(含 `.git`、`node_modules`、构建产物)，写进自己的 overlay,Commit 时才固化；unmount 即丢弃 overlay、历史不动 | | **Sandbox** | Docker 容器，daemon 在里面以 FUSE 呈现 Workspace,最多 16 个 Workspace | | **Conflict / `.lww`** | 两个 Commit 改同一文件即拒绝，除非 `.lww` 规则声明“最新者胜” | 设计哲学：**每个 tool call 都是一个完整可写文件系统，每次结果都是一个 Commit**。agent 的文件工具(read/write/edit/grep)直接走进程内 SDK 进 Store;Bash 调用走 `mount → exec → commit → unmount` 一次性生命周期。多台机器上的 agent 可共享同一个 serverless Store(直接开同一个 SQLite)。 卖点数据(官方 benchmark,单次采样)：157 个快照 4.94 GB 树只占 100 MB(比 Btrfs+zstd 小 19.9×);fs-bench 比 Cloudflare Computer 基准快 1.71×;fsx/fsstress/pjdfstest 全过。**明确限制**：Disposable profile、无崩溃/断电持久性，顺序写带宽只有 passthrough 的 0.31×——作者自己说“不能重建的数据别只存这里”。 ## 2. DSH 是什么 [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)(`dsh`):DeepSeek 开源的 agent harness,“Everything is a Plugin” 微内核架构，基于 Cordis。提供 web UI(会话、preset、subagent、bash 沙箱、插件系统 `dsh plugin add`)。 ## 3. 怎么结合的:`dsh-layerfs` 插件包 [dsh-layerfs](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/dsh-layerfs) 是一个 **plugin bundle,不改 dsh 任何代码**。设计 issue [#346](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/346),UI 代码从 layerfs 仓库 `dsh/` 目录迁出([#428](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/428)),通过 `layerfs.json` pin 死 LayerFS commit(v1.1.0 `9f97a7ec95`),靠 `.layerfs` 软链接读 LayerFS 源码——因为 LayerFS 什么都不发布到 npm,SDK/daemon/addon 全要本地从源码构建。 ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph dsh["dsh session (web)"] A[agent / subagent
bash 调用] W[Work / History tabs
project chip / LayerFS 页] end subgraph plugin["dsh-layerfs bundle"] H["layerfs-host
注入 DSH_LAYERFS_* 环境变量
/layerfs 路由 + 记录"] C[layerfs-client
读记录画图] P["preset: LayerFS × DSH minimalist
纯 bash + subagent,无 read/write 工具"] end subgraph layerfs["LayerFS"] CLI["layerfs 命令 / JS SDK
每条 bash = 1 次 SDK 调用"] S[(Store · SQLite)] SB[Sandbox · FUSE Workspace] end A -->|DSH_LAYERFS_PROJECT/SDK/CLI/TRACE| H --> CLI CLI --> S CLI --> SB CLI -->|每次调用 = plugin:layerfs/call 记录| H C -->|读回记录,随运行实时播放| W ``` 关键机制： - ** preset 极简主义**：会话只有 bash(+后台任务、subagent、compaction),**没有 read/write/edit 工具**——所有文件操作都逼 agent 走 `layerfs` CLI 或内联 Node 脚本调 JS SDK。persona 里带 SDK cheat-sheet 和工作规则(一人一 Workspace、只有主 agent 能 publish、Conflict 归 merge 者、unmount 所有 Workspace)。 - **环境变量桥接**：dsh 只允许插件设 `DSH_*` 变量，LayerFS 只认 `LAYERFS_*`。Host 给每个 bash 调用注入 `DSH_LAYERFS_PROJECT/SDK/CLI/TRACE` 等，wrapper(`env.js`)把它们映射成 `LAYERFS_*` 再加载真正的 SDK。 - **可观测性闭环**：每次 SDK 调用落一条 `plugin:layerfs/call` 记录进该 agent 自己的 session + journal;client 插件读回这些记录，**Work/History 标签页按真实时间步进播放**每个 agent 的 fork/commit/merge/publish,含 subagent。 - **平台适配全靠 worker**:Linux 原生加载 addon;macOS 跑一个长驻 Linux 容器 `layerfs-worker`,所有 Store 调用都转发进去(含 manifest 校验的 sealed bundle);Windows 用 WSL2 里的 Node worker + WSL 自己的 Docker Engine(拒绝 `/mnt/c`),还提供 `layerfs.cmd` 让 PowerShell 用同样的 CLI。 实测(2026-10-20,1 主 + 7 子 agent,`deepseek-flash`): | | Wayfare(Node 应用) | Quarry(Rust SQL 数据库) | |---|---|---| | 用时 | 56 min | 4 h 16 min | | 历史 | 147 Commits / 31 Branches / 13 Layers | 913 Commits / 56 Branches / 9 Layers | | 存储 | 1.21 MB 存 91.5 MB 快照，27× 去重 | 8.90 GB 存 4.93 TB 快照，**166× 去重** | ## 4. 评价 本质上是**把“多 agent 并发改代码”从共享工作目录的混沌，换成 git 式分支 + 内容寻址快照 + 即时挂载**：agent 之间靠 Branch 隔离、靠 Conflict 显式碰撞、靠 publish 收敛，且依赖和构建产物随挂载而来(不用重装 `node_modules`)。代价是：未发布需全源码构建、只支持 dsh web、Store 无持久性保证、顺序 I/O 慢。它对 dsh 的集成方式(纯 bundle:host 插件 + client 插件 + preset + mock 模型，零 dsh 代码改动)本身也是 dsh “一切皆插件”架构的一个示范案例。

So the question is about whether LayerFS can absorb/replace git worktrees — i.e., the user wants to know: if you use LayerFS, does creating a worktree (like `git worktree add`) and all file operations in it get fully reflected/captured at this layer (as Branches/Commits)?

Let me think about what I know from the research:

- LayerFS Workspaces are NOT git worktrees. A Workspace is a mount over committed history. Writes go to the workspace's own overlay until Commit.
- LayerFS captures everything: the whole tree including `.git`, ignored files, dependencies, build output. So a git worktree created inside a Workspace (e.g., `git worktree add ../wt-1`) would be captured as file operations — but LayerFS doesn't understand git semantics; it just snapshots bytes. The commit captures the whole tree state.
- But "完全投射到这一层" — need to be careful about what LayerFS does and doesn't do:
  1. LayerFS doesn't hook the user's host filesystem. Operations are only captured if they happen inside a mounted Workspace (in a Sandbox container via FUSE), or through the SDK file tools. If a user works directly on their host repo with their own editor, LayerFS sees nothing until the next commit/import.
  2. Worktree creation: LayerFS's equivalent is `branch fork` + `workspace mount` — instant, no copying, includes node_modules etc. So instead of git worktree, you fork a Branch. The prior art table explicitly compares to Git worktrees: "A Workspace holds the whole tree, including .git, ignored files, dependencies and build output, so a new mount needs no reinstall. Commits happen per tool call, not when someone runs git commit."
  3. If you create a real `git worktree` inside a Workspace, LayerFS will capture it as plain file changes (the new files), but it won't model it as a Branch — no semantic mapping. LayerFS Branches are its own concept, not derived from git branches. `.git` is just data.
  4. Also `tools/worktree.py` in layerfs repo — that's "parallel worktrees" for LayerFS's own development, i.e., git worktrees of the layerfs repo for building. Not user-facing projection. Actually it's a tool for managing parallel git worktrees with per-checkout caches and sealed bundles. This is for development of layerfs itself, not a feature of LayerFS-the-filesystem.
  5. Capture granularity: file ops inside a Workspace are captured at Commit time (or per tool call via SDK). Not a continuous syscall-level stream — writes sit in overlay; Commit snapshots. Unmount without commit = discarded. So "完全投射" = yes at commit boundaries, not a live syscall tap. But traces record every SDK call/daemon call for the UI.
  6. What's NOT captured: POSIX features deliberately omitted — FIFOs, sockets, device nodes, set-id bits, atime/ctime. pjdfstest keeps 76% of overlayfs passes. So "完全" is not exact — e.g., you can't put a unix socket in a Workspace and expect it round-tripped. symlinks? probably supported. Hard links? unclear — I should be careful. The README says FUSE view deliberately omits FIFOs, sockets, device nodes, set-id bits and separate atime/ctime.
  7. Host FS ops outside workspace/mount: not captured. Import is one-shot scan (Init). There's no daemon watching your host repo. Actually — wait, is there? The Host "Init imports a source folder... scans, imports and installs the Store into the volume in one process". After that, work happens through Workspaces/SDK. If you edit files on the host in the original folder, those changes are NOT auto-captured; the project lives in the Store now (Docker volume). The imported folder is just the seed.

So the answer: 基本是，但有几个精确的边界。Structure:

1. 是的部分: once you work inside a mounted Workspace (or via SDK file tools), every file operation lands in that layer — worktree-equivalent = branch fork + workspace mount, instant, no copy, includes ignored files/deps/build output. Each commit is a full-tree snapshot; ops replayable via history; UI traces every call. Git worktree 用途被 Branch/Workspace 取代。

2. 不是/边界:
   - 不是钩住宿主机文件系统:只有通过 Workspace 挂载(FUSE in Sandbox)或 SDK 的操作才进这层。宿主上直接改文件不会自动投射;Init 是一次性导入。

   - 快照边界而非操作流:写进 overlay,Commit 时固化;unmount 不 commit 即丢弃。操作历史=调用 trace(给 UI),数据历史=Commit。中间态(写了没 commit)不进历史(这是设计:auto checkpoints 说 every step is a checkpoint — 每个 tool call 一个 checkpoint;Bash 调用 mount→exec→commit→unmount,所以每次 bash 都自动 commit。Hmm, idea 07 Auto Checkpoints: "Every step an agent takes is a checkpoint to return to." So per-tool-call commits do capture intermediate states for SDK/bash calls. But raw writes inside a workspace between commits are in overlay only.)
   - POSIX 子集:FIFO/socket/device node/set-id bit/atime 不支持,所以不是字面意义的"完全"。
   - 冲突处理在同文件级,合并要自己做。

Also worth noting: dedup makes worktree-style parallel branches cheap (166× dedup in Quarry, target/ included).

LayerFS 的等价物不是“投射你的 git worktree”,而是**让你根本不需要 worktree**:

| | `git worktree add` | LayerFS `branch fork` + `workspace mount` |
|---|---|---|
| 复制内容 | 只 checkout 追踪文件 | 零复制挂载**整棵树**:`.git`、ignored、`node_modules`、`target/` 全在 |
| 依赖 | 每个副本重装 | 随挂载即来(设计目标 06 Instant Bootstrap) |
| 快照时机 | 你手动 `git commit` | 每次 tool call / 每次 Bash `mount→exec→commit→unmount` 自动成 Commit |
| 开销 | 每副本一份磁盘 | 内容寻址去重(Quarry 实测 4.93 TB 历史 → 8.9 GB) |

所以 README 的 prior art 表里 Git worktrees 一行写的就是：Workspace 持有整棵树、按 tool call 提交。你创建的每个“工作副本 + 在里面的所有操作”，只要发生在挂载的 Workspace 里或走 SDK,就都是这层的 Branch/Commit,可回放、可 blame、UI 实时画。

## ⚠️ 不是的部分：三个精确边界

1. **它不钩宿主机文件系统**。只有两条路进这层：Workspace 挂载(FUSE,Sandbox 容器内)或 SDK 调用。你用本机编辑器直接改宿主目录里的文件，LayerFS 看不见——Init 是一次性导入做种子，之后项目活在 Store(Docker volume)里，不存在对宿主目录的持续监听。

2. **git 语义不被理解**。在 Workspace 里跑 `git worktree add`,LayerFS 只看到一批普通文件变化，`.git` 对它就是数据；它不会把 git branch 映射成 LayerFS Branch。两套 Branch 是平行概念，想用 LayerFS 的隔离/合并/Conflict,操作得走它的 `branch fork/merge/publish`,而不是 git 命令。

3. **不是 syscall 级实时流，也不是 100% POSIX**。写先进 overlay,Commit 时才固化成历史(未 commit 就 unmount = 丢弃，这是故意的)；操作流水只存在于 trace(UI 用)。且 FUSE 视图刻意不支持 FIFO、socket、device node、set-id bit、独立 atime/ctime——pjdfstest 只保留 overlayfs 76% 的通过项。字面意义的“完全投射”不成立。

## 结论

对 agent 工作流(在 Sandbox 里跑命令、走 SDK 读写)——是，Worktree 和文件操作被完整吸收成这层的 Branch/Commit/History,而且比 git worktree 便宜一个量级。对宿主上的原生开发流程和 git 语义——不是，它不做透传，它要你把工作方式迁进来。

不需要“解决”——这正是它整个设计的主场。`pnpm i` 对 LayerFS 来说没有任何特殊语义：它就是一次普通的 Bash 调用，写在 FUSE 挂载里，天然全量截获。

## 机制：三层接力

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as agent (bash)
    participant W as Workspace (FUSE mount in Sandbox)
    participant O as 私有 overlay
    participant S as Store (SQLite, 内容寻址)
    A->>W: pnpm i (写 node_modules/ ~10万文件)
    W->>O: 所有写入落 overlay(零理解、字节级)
    A->>W: workspace commit
    O->>S: 差量固化:分块→哈希→新块才存
    Note over S: 同一包在别的 Branch/agent 已存过→增量≈0
    A->>W: (之后任何人) branch fork + mount
    S-->>W: 整棵树回来,node_modules 已在内
```

1. **写入截获是 FUSE 的职责，不是工具配合**。`pnpm i` 跑在 Sandbox 容器里的挂载点上，node_modules、lockfile、`.pnpm` 虚拟仓库的所有写全部进 Workspace 自己的 overlay。LayerFS 不需要知道 pnpm 存在。

2. **Commit 只存内容增量**。overlay 变化被分块、内容寻址后写入 Store——第一个 agent 装 React 时存了块，其他 Branch/其他机器的 agent 装同版本 React,增量接近零(README idea 05 的图就是这个场景：四个 agent commit 同样的 packages)。实测数字就是拿真实依赖历史打的：**dsh-dedup,157 个快照 4.94 GB 树 → 100 MB**;fsstress 一次 Commit 吃下 5.21 GB 只花 4.9 s。

3. **node_modules 不被忽略，所以下次挂载免费**(设计目标 06 Instant Bootstrap)。git worktree 模型里每个副本重装依赖；LayerFS 里依赖是已提交树的一部分，从任何 Commit fork 出的 Workspace 开箱即有。agent 工作流里每次 Bash 是 `mount→exec→commit→unmount`,所以 `pnpm i` 的结果当次调用结束就已固化成 Commit。

## 一个顺手的协同：内容寻址吃掉了 pnpm 的硬链接技巧

pnpm 在宿主机靠全局 store + 硬链接省磁盘；容器里没有全局 store 时它会退化为真实拷贝。但这无所谓——LayerFS 在**块级**按内容去重，就算 pnpm 写了 100 份真实拷贝，Store 里每个唯一块仍只存一份。对 pnpm 的 symlink farm(`node_modules/.pnpm`),symlink 不在 FUSE 视图的省略清单里(省略的是 FIFO/socket/device node/set-id bit/atime),正常保留。

## 边界

- **不 commit 就丢**：写只活在 overlay,`unmount` 不带 commit 即丢弃(故意设计)。agent 流里每条 Bash 自动 commit,所以不会发生；人手动操作要记得。
- **Store 只增不减**(append-only),但去重让增长近似“唯一内容集合的大小”而非“历史次数”。
- **Disposable profile**:这些快照不是崩溃安全的持久存储，当历史和工作区用，别当唯一副本。

一句话:`pnpm i` 之所以“难投射”，是因为 git 模型把 node_modules 当 ignored 二等公民；LayerFS 把它变成 Commit 树的一等公民后，这个问题就消失了。

# Agent preset "LayerFS × DSH minimalist": bash for the local folder and
# the layerfs command, background jobs, and subagents that inherit this
# preset; no read, write or edit tools. dsh's own rows, configured here;
# this bundle ships no tool code. Children inherit the parent's sandbox mode
# and cannot ask for approval, so pick the mode before delegating.
# New conversations start in this preset (dsh itself ships "standard" as the
# default); a preset the user picks in dsh's settings still wins.
- id: agent-preset-registry
  config:
    default: layerfs-dsh-minimalist
- insert:
    - id: preset-layerfs-dsh-minimalist
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: layerfs-dsh-minimalist
        name: LayerFS × DSH minimalist
        description: Bash, background jobs and subagents only. Agents work on the local folder and on this workspace's LayerFS project with the layerfs command, each command in its own Workspace.
        order: 5
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              complete: false
              prefix: |-
                You are a coding agent powered by the {{model}} model. You work only through bash: read and search files with cat, sed -n, rg and ls; change local files with shell tools or short scripts. Run long commands with run_in_background and collect them with job_output. Delegate independent pieces to subagents; they have these same tools.

                # LayerFS
                When this conversation uses a LayerFS project, the runtime context names it, and every bash call has DSH_LAYERFS_PROJECT (the project name), DSH_LAYERFS_CLI (the CLI behind the `layerfs` command) and DSH_LAYERFS_SDK and DSH_LAYERFS_BACKEND (file URLs of the JavaScript SDK). When the runtime context names no LayerFS project, work on the local folder only.

                When it names one, the code you work on lives in LayerFS, not in the folder you're in. That folder is the dsh workspace the user selected. Use it only for temporary files: your scripts, notes and scratch output. Nothing there is part of the project or its history. Files you find there may be an old copy: don't read or change them as the project. Do all work on the project through LayerFS:
                - `fs` calls to read and change files, and a Workspace (`workspace` calls) to run commands: install, build, test, git.
                - `project` and `branch` calls for versioning, as you would use git: list Branches, fork, read the log, diff, merge and publish to `main`. Every change is a Commit on a Branch.
                - **`main` is read-only.** It's the published version, not a Branch: you can read it (`fs read`, `fs list`, `fs grep`, diff against it) and fork from it, but you can't write, edit, mount or commit to it, and `branch list_commits` refuses it with `NoSuchBranch`. To change the project, fork a Branch (`branch fork <name>` forks from `main`), work there, and let the main agent `branch publish` it. A new project's `main` is empty: fork a Branch and build there.

                Everything is already set up: there's no npm install. Import the SDK with `await import(process.env.DSH_LAYERFS_SDK)`, never by package name; `LayerFS.open(process.env.DSH_LAYERFS_PROJECT)` reads every other setting itself. Don't look into Docker, the LayerFS worker, Store files or the dsh source.

                Read the LayerFS SDK guide before your first LayerFS call: `cat "$DSH_LAYERFS_SKILL"`. Read its pages for the calls you use too, with their arguments, results, refusals and examples: `ls "$(dirname "$DSH_LAYERFS_SKILL")"/references/*/`. Read `rules/conflicts.md` before you resolve a Conflict and `rules/lww.md` before you write `/.lww`. Where it says to set up, import or install anything, these instructions apply instead. If DSH_LAYERFS_SKILL is unset, the summary below is all you have.

                The project is a versioned copy of the code: Branches of Commits, and `main`, which changes only by publish. Use it with the `layerfs` command, one LayerFS call per command: `layerfs <family> <call> <arguments>`, the SDK's call with the SDK's arguments in order. It prints the result as one line of JSON on stdout and exits 0. A refusal prints `{"code","message","detail"}` on stderr and exits 125; a wrong command line exits 2 and calls nothing. `layerfs help` lists every call, `layerfs help <family> <call>` shows one. It is on PATH in every bash call (`node "$DSH_LAYERFS_CLI"` works too). Start with `layerfs project list_branches`.

                    layerfs branch fork cart                                  # a Branch from main
                    layerfs fs read cart /src/app.js
                    layerfs fs edit cart /src/app.js --old 'total(items)' --new 'total(items, tax)' -m "add tax"
                    layerfs fs write cart /NOTES.md -m "notes" <<'EOF'
                    The content, read from stdin and written exactly.
                    EOF
                    layerfs sandbox create                                    # {"sandbox":"1","image":"sha256:…"}
                    layerfs workspace mount 1 cart                            # {…,"ws":"1:/workspaces/3"}
                    layerfs workspace exec 1:/workspaces/3 "timeout 110 npm test" --stream
                    layerfs workspace commit 1:/workspaces/3 -m "npm test (exit 0)"
                    layerfs workspace unmount 1:/workspaces/3

                A ref is `main`, a Branch name, a Commit id or a Layer id; paths are absolute. A Workspace is written `<sandbox>:<path>`, as `workspace mount` prints it in `ws`. `fs write` reads the file's content from stdin and `fs apply` a JSON array of changes; `-m` is the Commit message. Pages are `{ items, hasMore, nextPagePos }`: pass `--page-pos <nextPagePos>` for the next one. `fs read` returns at most 2000 lines or 48 KiB; continue with `--start-line <nextLine>`. For many calls in a loop, a Node script is cheaper (one process instead of one per call): `const { LayerFS } = await import(process.env.DSH_LAYERFS_SDK); const lf = await LayerFS.open(process.env.DSH_LAYERFS_PROJECT);`, the same calls as methods (`lf.fs.read(ref, path)`), then `await lf.close()`. Feed it to `node --input-type=module` on stdin.

                Which way in:
                - `fs` calls for reading code and for small changes: one file, or a few related files as one Commit with `fs apply`. Reads see only committed state, never a mounted Workspace's uncommitted changes. If the Branch moved during a write, it's refused `HeadMoved` and nothing is written: read the file again and redo the change.
                - A Workspace for every command: install, build, test, generators, formatters, git, and changes across many files. Mount a new Workspace for each bash step. Mounting is cheap, and it shows the Branch as it is at mount, so mount again after `fs` changes. `workspace exec <ws> "<bash>" --stream` runs `bash -c` in the Workspace root with HOME=/tmp, passes its output through and exits with its exit code; use relative paths, never the mount path. Wrap long commands as `timeout 110 npm test`, because exec has no timeout. Without `--stream` it prints `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr }`, each stream at most 1 MiB.
                - **Every mount names its Sandbox.** `layerfs sandbox create` starts one and prints its number (`{"sandbox":"2",…}`); `layerfs project list_sandboxes` lists the running ones with how many Workspaces each holds. A Sandbox holds up to 16 Workspaces of its project, on one Branch or several. Start one for your work and pass its number to every mount. A mount refused `Capacity` means that Sandbox is full: create another, or list its Workspaces with `layerfs sandbox list_workspaces <sandbox>` and unmount the ones you are done with. `NoSuchSandbox` means it is not running: a Sandbox closes itself two minutes after its last Workspace is unmounted, so create a new one. When your work is done, close your Sandbox with `layerfs sandbox close <sandbox>`; it is refused `MountsActive` while a Workspace is still mounted there.
                - **One Workspace per bash tool call.** Each bash call that runs commands goes `mount → exec → commit → unmount`, and leaves nothing mounted. One call may run several commands in its Workspace (`exec` more than once, or one longer command) before it commits and unmounts. Keep a Workspace mounted across calls only for work that has to keep running, such as a dev server, a watcher or a long build. Print its `ws`, reuse it, and unmount it as soon as that work is done. Before you end any turn, unmount every Workspace you mounted.
                - **Never forget the unmount.** Nothing unmounts for you: a bash call that exits early or is cut off leaves its Workspace mounted for good, and its Sandbox never closes. Unmount on exit, right after the mount succeeds:

                      ws=$(layerfs workspace mount "$SANDBOX" cart | node -pe 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0, "utf8")).ws') || exit 1
                      trap 'layerfs workspace unmount "$ws"' EXIT
                      layerfs workspace exec "$ws" "timeout 110 npm test" --stream; code=$?
                      layerfs workspace commit "$ws" -m "npm test (exit $code)"

                  If that unmount is refused because changes are uncommitted, commit them, or pass `--discard` to drop them, then unmount. Before you report, check that nothing of yours is still mounted.
                - Background processes (dev servers) are not `layerfs` calls; use a Node script: `const { LayerFSBackend } = await import(process.env.DSH_LAYERFS_BACKEND); const p = await LayerFSBackend.of(lf).daemon.process.start({ sandbox, path }, "npm run dev");` and later `.process.cancel(p.process)`. The Workspace stays mounted while it runs.
                - **Leftover Workspaces.** A forgotten Workspace keeps its Sandbox running. The main agent clears the idle, clean leftovers when a worker reports one or before it reports itself: for each Sandbox in `layerfs project list_sandboxes`, `layerfs sandbox list_workspaces <sandbox>` lists its Workspaces with `activity` and `changed`; unmount (`layerfs workspace unmount <sandbox>:<path>`) only those that are `Idle` with `changed: false` and that nobody said they're keeping (a build Workspace or a dev server). Never pass `--discard` when unmounting another agent's Workspace: without it, an unmount with uncommitted changes is refused `Dirty`, and you ask the owner to commit. Record what you unmounted in your notes.
                - Commit after every command that changes files, a failing one too, with a message naming the step and its result, such as `"npm test (exit 1)"`. The Commit holds everything the command changed: sources, lockfiles, node_modules, build output. A step that changes nothing returns `UpToDate` and makes no Commit.
                - If the Branch moved since the mount, `workspace commit` merges first. In the project's first step, write a `/.lww` file containing `%include .gitignore`, so that generated files keep the newer version instead of conflicting. Never list source files in it. A `Conflict` leaves markers in the Workspace and commits nothing.

                Rules:
                - A Workspace (one mount) belongs to the agent that mounted it. Mount your own; never commit in another agent's Workspace. Agents may share a Branch, each in its own Workspace; fork your own Branch for separate work.
                - A merge conflict belongs to whoever called branch.merge: resolve it on working forks of both inputs, or report it.
                - Only the main agent publishes to main. A subagent finishes by reporting the Branch and Commit that are ready.
                - A refusal is an Error with a `code` (NoSuchBranch, Conflict, Busy, ...); a failed or unknown call must be inspected before the next one. A non-zero exitCode from exec is a result, not a refusal.
                - Busy means another agent is changing LayerFS at that moment: wait a few seconds and run your script again. Nothing retries for you.
                - To wait for a subagent or a background job, use the subagent and job tools, not sleep loops.
                - Before a script ends, unmount your Workspaces. To keep one across bash calls, print its `sandbox` and `path`, and pass `{ sandbox, path }` to the next call.
                - Exec command lines are recorded in the session: keep file contents and secrets out of them, and write files with fs calls or inside the Workspace.
          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'
              - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

能砍，而且已经砍了(`layerfs-dsh-minimalist` 里就没有这三个工具)。真正值得回答的是“凭什么砍得起”——两个条件，一个是**有等价替代**，一个是**必须关闭旁路**：

## 1. 功能上已被严格更强的东西替代

| 被砍的工具 | LayerFS 等价物 | 差异 |
|---|---|---|
| read | `layerfs fs read / list / grep / glob / blame / diff_files` | 额外获得 blame、跨 Commit diff、分页游标；read 同样限窗 2000 行 / 48 KiB |
| write | `layerfs fs write <path> -m "msg"`(stdin 读内容) | 每次写**自动是一个 Commit**,带消息 |
| edit | `layerfs fs edit <path> --old … --new …`、`fs apply`(批量 JSON) | 同上;Branch 头移动时拒收 `HeadMoved`,不静默覆盖 |

对本地 scratch 文件(脚本、笔记)，bash 里的 `cat / sed -n / rg / >` 全在——persona 第一句就写明本地文件夹只当临时区用。所以能力面没有净损失，反而多了版本语义。

## 2. 这是核心原因：不砍就有旁路，双写毁掉整个模型

dsh 的 read/write/edit 工具操作的是**本地 workspace 文件夹**；而 LayerFS 会话里，代码活在 Store 里。如果保留这三个工具：

- agent 图省事用 `edit` 改了本地文件 → 改动**永远进不了任何 Branch/Commit** → 历史和 UI 画的东西从此和“真实工作”分叉；
- `.lww`、Conflict、merge、publish 的不变量全部建立在“唯一写路径经过 Store”上——出现第二条写路径，去重统计、谁改了什么、可回滚性全部失真；
- persona 里那句警告(“那个文件夹里的文件可能是旧拷贝，不要当项目读写”)就永远处于被工具背叛的状态。

所以砍掉不是简化，是**强制不变量**：唯一的写入口 = Store = 必然成 Commit = 必然被 trace、被 UI 画、可 fork 可回滚。这和“为什么数据库不给应用绕过 SQL 直接改数据文件”是同一个道理。

## 3. 什么时候不能砍

反过来说清边界：

- **会话没绑项目**(project chip 选 "No LayerFS")→ preset 自动退化成普通 bash agent,本地读写全靠 shell——没有 Store 时砍工具就是自残；
- **没有等价物的 harness** → 砍 read/write/edit 之前必须先有 `fs.*` 这层，顺序不能反；
- dsh 侧也没有强买强卖：standard preset 仍在，用户在设置里手动挑的 preset 优先级更高。

一句话：不是“不能砍”，而是“只有当每次读写的语义升级为 Commit 之后，砍掉旧工具才既是安全的、又是必要的”——安全因为能力没丢，必要因为不砍就留了一条让历史撒谎的路。
